purpose: One thing an observer saw, written so anyone can check it and nobody can change it.
principle: Its id is a hash of what it says, written one canonical way. Spell a set in another order and the id stays. Erase the payload and the id, the signature and every record that cites it still hold.
eg: Every card in the walk is a record.
state: An envelope, a payload and a signature. A fold reads the payload's top-level fields: a list reads as a set, no field name is special, and nothing reads inside a nested object.

principle: Nothing a record says is true. It is said, by its observer. Two observers who disagree leave two records, and both are kept.
eg: Rosa, Ben and Kim in the walk.
state: A typed reference on every record. Today it is the signing key, k:…, checked on every read.
note: Lineages (sl:…), key bindings and standing come in step 3. What an observer names is open: IS10 and IS11.

purpose: Gives each subject its own state.
principle: Inside a thing, a record that nothing replaces is a head. Two records that replace the same one make a fork. A record that names both heads merges them.
state: A typed name, prefix:value, in a record's of: a natural key or a record id. Every record is of exactly one thing. A record with no of and no prev is a root and starts a thing named by its own id. about only mentions other things.

purpose: Holds records, and nothing else. It owns no meaning.
principle: A store is a set. Read its places in any order and you keep the same records, once per id.
state: A set of records kept in places, each record one canonical line.

purpose: Lets readers who hold different payloads still agree on what is current.
principle: Missing payloads never change which records are heads. Where a fold can't read a payload, it says how many it couldn't read.
eg: Kim's copy, which holds E without its payload.
state: What one reader holds: each record with its payload, withheld, or erased. Envelopes are always held.

purpose: A standing question, written as data anyone can check.
principle: An accepted spec parses back to itself. A refused one names the first rule it breaks, and where.
state: vertex names it, from lists its sources, fold lists its slots.

purpose: Chooses records by their envelopes alone.
principle: A source takes a record when its kind is listed, it mentions the thing in about, and it is of the thing in of, each only when given. A reader with fewer payloads takes exactly the same records.
state: A store, then optionally kinds, a thing it mentions (about) and the thing it is of.

principle: The same records give every slot the same value, whatever order they came in. A slot over heads returns only records that are still heads. A slot with by splits into groups and accounts for every record it selected.
state: A name and one fold, optionally with where, follow, limit and by.

purpose: Turns a set of records into state.
principle: The read path hands each record over once, so a fold can take new records as they arrive and still reach the same state.
eg: latest-by picks the current recipe; count counts its versions.
state: One of six: count, sum, min, max, latest-by, collect. Following prev, a fold runs over each thing's heads. Following keys, it reads each thing by its live setters. Otherwise it runs over every selected record. The proofs over heads use cached latest-by state, not just a cached answer.

purpose: Asks a standing question over stores: select, fold, tick.
principle: Run it over the same set and it gives the same slots, each with a count of the records it couldn't read.
state: A spec, run over what a reader holds.
note: Settled and not built: naming a vertex by its spec's hash, and when it ticks.

purpose: Fixes a vertex's result at a moment, so others can cite it.
principle: Anyone who holds the covered records works out the same tick.
eg: Step 8 of the walk: one tick covering five records.
state: An ordinary record of kind tick: the vertex, the exact records it covers, and the result, with an id over all three. A tick folds a set named outright, a part closed downward over prev, or a slice of one.
note: Built in the model with its laws and vectors, in Rust, and in the CLI: loops tick writes one, and loops tick --check answers same, differs or cannot check. A tick made on one machine checks the same on another, and can cover a cut by time or by ids. Not built yet: boundaries, markers and the runner. The tick record note.

purpose: Turns state into text people edit, and edits back into records.
principle: Render, then parse, and you get the document back. Drop a section from the text and that section keeps its old body: leaving something out is never an edit.
eg: Step 9 of the walk, where Ben edits a section.
state: A render, a parse and a diff by ids, and the base the text came from.
note: Sections need nonempty, distinct ids. The edit round trip also keeps exactly the base's ordered list of ids. Emitting accepted edits is planned.

purpose: Gives standing ahead of time, with a scope.
principle: A record without standing stays visible, and has no effect.
eg: Rosa's grant to Ben to write recipes in the family store.
state: A record. A record that acts on it names it in under.
note: What a grant holds, how it ends and who may give one wait on IS3, IS4, IS5 and IS7.
